With high error correlation (0.913), unstable ranking (Kendall tau 0.329), and only 3 validation windows making any fitted weighting high-variance, there's no compelling hypothesis that a different kind of strategy would meaningfully outperform this robust trimmed mean. action_args.justification: The series is trend-dominated with moderate seasonality and high inter-model error correlation (mean 0.913, only 1 independent group). Ranking is unstable across the 3 validation windows (Kendall tau 0.329, best model changes each window), which makes fitted weights or per-horizon selection high-variance. A trimmed mean over the 7 most stable models (pool2) is the right robust combination: it discards the most outlying forecasts while retaining the consensus of the correlated-but-slightly-different models. The leader is a seed baseline and the runner-up is statistically indistinguishable, so further tuning is unlikely to produce a real gain.
